import java.util.Scanner;

public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
        String s = sc.next();
        StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
        int n = s.length();

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (i + 3 <= n && s.substring(i, i + 3).equals("dot")) {
                result.append('.');
                i += 2;
            } else if (i + 2 <= n && s.substring(i, i + 2).equals("at")) {
                result.append('@');
                i += 1;
            } else {
                result.append(s.charAt(i));
            }
        }

        // Helper method to replace end character if it matches
        replaceEnd(result, '.', "dot");
        replaceEnd(result, '@', "at");

        int atCount = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < result.length(); i++) {
            if (result.charAt(i) == '@') {
                atCount++;
            }
        }

        if (atCount == 1) {
            System.out.println(result.toString());
        } else {
            boolean firstAt = true;
            StringBuilder output = new StringBuilder();
            for (int i = 0; i < result.length(); i++) {
                char ch = result.charAt(i);
                if (ch == '@') {
                    if (firstAt) {
                        output.append('@');
                        firstAt = false;
                    } else {
                        output.append("at");
                    }
                } else {
                    output.append(ch);
                }
            }
            System.out.println(output.toString());
        }
    }

    private static void replaceEnd(StringBuilder sb, char c, String replacement) {
        if (sb.length() > 0 && sb.charAt(sb.length() - 1) == c) {
            sb.deleteCharAt(sb.length() - 1);
            sb.append(replacement);
        }
    }
}
